questions.question: Materials that allow electricity to flow through them are called:
questions.explanation: Conductors allow electricity to flow easily. Most metals are good conductors.

questions.question: Which material is the best conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Silver is the best conductor of electricity, though copper is more commonly used.

questions.question: Insulators are used in electrical wires to:
questions.explanation: Insulating material (rubber/plastic) around wires prevents electrical shock and short circuits.

questions.question: Which of these is an insulator?
questions.explanation: Wood is a poor conductor of electricity — it is an insulator.

questions.question: A complete path for electricity to flow is called a:
questions.explanation: An electric circuit is a closed loop through which electric current flows.

questions.question: What happens in an open circuit?
questions.explanation: In an open circuit, the path is broken — no current flows and the bulb does not glow.

questions.question: Which device is used to make or break a circuit?
questions.explanation: A switch controls the circuit — open switch breaks the circuit, closed switch completes it.

questions.question: Why do birds sitting on power lines not get electrocuted?
options: Current flows only through one wire, birds don't complete a circuit to ground
questions.explanation: Birds on a single wire don't complete a circuit between two points of different potential, so no current flows through them.

questions.question: Graphite (pencil lead) is:
questions.explanation: Graphite is an unusual non-metal that conducts electricity due to its structure.

questions.question: In a torch, what converts electrical energy to light energy?
questions.explanation: The bulb (filament) converts electrical energy to light (and heat) energy.

questions.question: When metals are heated, they become:
questions.explanation: Generally, metals conduct electricity better at lower temperatures. However, metals remain conductors when heated.

questions.question: Which is NOT safe to do during a thunderstorm?
questions.explanation: Tall trees attract lightning. Standing under one during a storm is very dangerous.

questions.question: A fuse in an electric circuit:
options: Protects the circuit by melting when current is too high
questions.explanation: A fuse has a thin wire that melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds a safe level.

questions.question: Water conducts electricity because of:
questions.explanation: Pure water is a poor conductor; tap/sea water conducts because of dissolved mineral ions.

questions.question: Which material would make the best insulator for electrical cables?
questions.explanation: PVC (plastic) is an excellent electrical insulator — it covers copper wires to make safe cables.
